title: [D6 Orchestration] Ephemeral in-process state and re-run recovery
summary: `AssessmentStore.store` now supersedes every run over `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)` that the pass it is storing did not write, addressing the three identifiers a snapshot could ever hold (`helena.orchestration.RUNS_OF_A_PASS`) by key — which makes re-running an interrupted assessment well-defined even when the re-run routes differently, and collects the child rows a run killed between `_one`'s children and its assessment row leaves orphaned. The ephemeral-state half is now asserted by execution rather than by comment: the package writes no file anywhere, a whole assessment rebinds no name in any `helena` module, and a `SIGKILL`ed child process running one assessment leaves its home, its temporary directory and its working directory empty.
assumption_validated: That `concept/03`'s *"an interrupted run is simply re-run, because the versioned context already makes that correct rather than a fallback"* needs no recovery machinery — and it does not: no resume, no run registry, no lease and no checkpoint were added, and re-run is calling `assess` again over the same projection. But the claim did NOT hold as it stood. The identifier carries the trigger, so a re-run that routed differently from the run it replaced minted a different analyst identifier and left the earlier analyst row standing as a second live verdict over one context version; and a run killed between the child rows and the assessment row left orphans no join could reach. Both are now closed by the supersede step, and both were demonstrated failing first: the two new store tests fail with the call removed and pass with it.
makes_buildable: Task 45 (assessment replay) can now assume that what the store holds for one `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)` is what the last completed pass over it produced and nothing else — one triage row, at most one analyst row, and child rows only under identifiers that have a parent. That is the precondition a replay reads against, and without it a replay could have found two analyst rows with different triggers and no rule for choosing. `RUNS_OF_A_PASS` is also the enumeration a reader needs: the three identifiers a snapshot could hold are a pure function of the request, so a replay can address them by key without a scan. Task 46/47 (the sink) get the same guarantee for the one-message-per-terminal-outcome join — the pass's two rows are the only two. The unowned gap from task 43 is UNCHANGED and still unowned: the escalation is not stored, so a routing replay is sound only while the thresholds have not moved.

verification.detail: 1648 passed, 1 skipped (the skip is tests/test_agents.py's live-endpoint one, pre-existing). Everything touching the store ran against the real RisingWave 3.0.3 instance: the supersede is executed SQL, and the interrupted-run test produces real orphaned rows with a connection that stops mid-write. Both new store tests were confirmed to FAIL with `_supersede` commented out and pass with it, so they test the change rather than describe it. The killed-run test spawns a real child process against a real loopback endpoint that never answers and asserts the exit status is -SIGKILL, so nothing had the chance to tidy up.

deferred: RESUMABILITY. Not built, and the terms are unchanged from ADR-0032 §6: the number that would decide it is the observed rate of interrupted runs times the quota a repeat burns, and nothing has been measured. What this increment changes is that the cost of a re-run is now only the repeated work, with no leftover rows to reconcile. The compatible form of a checkpoint is still typed rows in the single store keyed by (context reference, context version, trigger) — never a framework's backend.

A READ PATH. Task 43 deferred one and this increment did not add one: the supersede addresses identifiers by key and never reads the store, precisely so it did not have to invent the versioned reader task 45 needs.
THE ESCALATION RECORD. Still not stored and still owned by no task. Unchanged by this increment; see `helena.orchestration`'s "what is deliberately not here" and ADR-0033 §7.
PRUNING AND RETENTION. Superseding is not pruning — it removes the rows of a run that was replaced and bounds nothing. `concept/08` still lists the retention horizon as open.

A COUNTER FOR SUPERSEDED ROWS. `store` returns the identifiers it wrote, as before, and the supersede is silent. It is the same semantics as the upsert that was already silent for the row whose key does not change, and making one of the two countable and not the other would have been arbitrary. If D8's metrics want 'how often did a re-run route differently', that is a decision with a shape (a log record, or a returned tuple) and it belongs to whoever needs the number.
lessons: AN IDENTIFIER THAT CARRIES A ROUTING DECISION MAKES IDEMPOTENCE PER-ROW, NOT PER-PASS. `assessment_id` includes the trigger, which is right — it is what says why analysis ran — but it means a re-run that routed differently does not address the row it is replacing, and an upsert cannot delete a row it is not addressing. The generalisation worth carrying: whenever an identifier includes something a re-run may legitimately decide differently, idempotence has to be enforced at the level of the thing that is being re-run (here, the pass over one context snapshot), not at the level of the key.

THE CLEANUP NEEDS NO READ PATH BECAUSE THE KEY SPACE IS ENUMERABLE. `helena.contracts.v1.AgentRequest` accepts exactly three (emitter, trigger) pairings, so the three identifiers one context version could ever hold are a pure function of the request. Addressing them by key rather than by a `SELECT` avoids the versioned reader task 45 still owes, avoids a FLUSH-ordering question inside the writer, and — the part that mattered — reaches ORPHANED CHILD ROWS, which a query keyed on what is present would never find because their parent row does not exist.

'NO DURABLE IN-FLIGHT STATE OUTSIDE THE ENGINE' IS TESTABLE WITH A SIGKILLED CHILD PROCESS, AND CHEAPLY. The parent holds an endpoint that accepts the prompt and never answers, the child runs one assessment against it with HOME, TMPDIR and cwd pointed at three empty directories, and it is killed inside the first model call. Two details make it a proof rather than a gesture: assert the exit status IS -SIGKILL (an exception path would have run `finally` blocks and proved nothing), and set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE rather than allowing a .pyc exception — a test that allows one exception has to allow the next. `tests/test_orchestration.py::assess_at` is the module-level entry point the child imports.

COMPARING EVERY `helena.*` MODULE'S `__dict__` ACROSS A RUN NEEDS A WARM-UP RUN FIRST. Five modules (`contracts`, `policy`, `taxonomy`, `triage`, `rendering`, `hosts`) `import_module` their frozen version module on first use, which adds a name to the package's namespace. That is an import, not state, and without a preceding run the identity comparison fails on it. Run once, snapshot, run again, compare.

THE PACKAGE OPENS NO FILE FOR WRITING AT ALL, WHICH MAKES THE ASSERTION SIMPLE AND EXACT. `test_the_package_writes_no_file_anywhere` forbids `open`, the `Path` write/create methods, the `os` write calls and `tempfile`/`shutil` outright. Two false-positive traps found while writing it: `.replace(` and `.remove(` are string and list methods used all over the tree, so the `os` calls are matched only on an attribute whose value is the NAME `os`; and `helena.observability` calls `.write` on a stream ITS CALLER OPENED, which is why `write` is not on the list.
failed_approaches: Deriving the superseded set with a SELECT over the assessment table for the snapshot, and deleting what was found. Rejected before it was committed for two reasons, the second of which is the one that matters: it is a read path task 43 deliberately deferred (and a real one has to validate against the row's own `schema_version`), and it CANNOT SEE ORPHANED CHILD ROWS — the residue of a run killed between the children and the assessment row is exactly the case where no parent row exists to be found. Addressing the three derivable identifiers by key has neither problem.

Superseding before writing the pass's rows. Rejected: it would reopen the window ADR-0033 §1 closed by choosing to upsert the assessment row rather than delete-then-insert — an instant in which a context version has no assessment at all. The writes go first, the supersede second.
next_session_should_know: Task 45 is assessment replay, and this task's guarantee is the precondition it reads against. SIX THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THERE IS NO RE-RUN ENTRY POINT AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. Re-running an interrupted assessment is calling `orchestration.assess(...)` again over the same projection and storing the result; `concept/03` has no resume, and none was invented. If you go looking for `rerun`, `resume` or a run registry, they are absent on purpose — ADR-0034 §1. (2) `AssessmentStore.store` NOW DELETES ROWS, AND WHICH ONES IS EXACT: after writing the pass's one or two rows it removes every OTHER run over `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)`, addressing the three identifiers `orchestration.RUNS_OF_A_PASS` enumerates. So after any completed store, a snapshot holds one triage row, at most one analyst row, and child rows only under an identifier that has a parent. If you add a fourth (emitter, trigger) pairing to the contract, `test_the_runs_of_a_pass_are_exactly_the_pairings_the_contract_accepts` fails and it is telling you about a row nothing would ever collect. (3) THE ORDER IS WRITE-THEN-SUPERSEDE and it is load-bearing (no window with no assessment). Anything you add to `store` goes before the supersede or after it deliberately, not wherever it fits. (4) A RE-RUN IS IDEMPOTENT IN ITS RECORD, NOT IN ITS VERDICT. The model is not deterministic and nothing here makes it so; what is well-defined is that the store ends up holding the last completed pass. A replay that expects the same classification back is expecting something this project has never claimed. (5) THE EPHEMERAL-STATE PROPERTY IS THREE EXECUTED TESTS in `tests/test_orchestration.py`, not a comment: no file written anywhere in the package, no `helena.*` module rebinding a name across a whole assessment, and a SIGKILLed child leaving three empty directories. If you add a module that writes a file — a cache, a scratchpad, an export — the first of those fails, and that is the escalation firing, not a broken test. (6) THE RULE FOR A FRAMEWORK CONVENIENCE IS WRITTEN DOWN: ADR-0034 §4 has the three questions (single store / agents-propose / ephemeral state) to ask before switching one on, and what does NOT count as an argument. `helena.budgets.RunBudget` and `helena.disclosure.Disclosures` are the two in-process mutable objects that are fine, because they die with the call.
